newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No upper limit set on Brazil Brady swap-cenbank.
newsitem.headline: No upper limit set on Brazil Brady swap-cenbank.

text.p: Brazil has fixed no specific upper limit in its offer to swap Brady bonds for a 30-year global and to buy back some Brady debt, said Gustavo Franco, Central Bank Director of International Affairs.
Franco said the "theoretical" limit was the total $26 billion stock of restructured Bradies held by Brazil but "we don't even expect to get close to that".
Franco told reporters in Brasilia that the Central Bank had no intention of immediately selling off the zero-coupon Treasury bills, or strips, held as collateral for some Par and Discount Bradies.
"We aren't going to do that. What we want to avoid is being obliged to sell in one go a large chunk of this debt, getting a very poor price for it as a result," Franco said.
The Central Bank director said the strips amounted to about 22-23 percent of the face value of Brazil's $18 billion in Par and Discount Bradies.

Franco said he did not fear the simultaneous swap and buyback operation would be adversely affected by an ongoing votes-for-money scandal in Brazil. The operation remains open to offers until 1500 EDT/1900 GMT on June 3,
Bradies slipped last week after allegations deputies had been paid $190,000 to vote in favour of a re-election bill.

"We are very satisfied with the reception this morning in New York," Franco said. "I have not noticed any particular concern among investors (over the votes-for-money scam). Political scandals happen here as they do in any country. They (the investors) are more concerned with economic fundamentals."
The minimum size for the global is $1.0 billion and its minimum clearing spread, in a modified Dutch auction, was set at 300 basis points over U.S. Treasuries due 2026.
Asked what a reasonable final spread would be, Franco simply said, "That's the million-dollar question. We want it (the interest rate) to be as low as possible."
He added that Brazil's recent five-year global was trading at about 170 bp over equivalent Treasuries.
